plan: In a second-price auction (pay second-highest bid if I win), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds both competitors' bids (guaranteeing non-negative profit) and lose otherwise, avoiding overpaying. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no incentive to shade up or down. With no prior history in this single-round game, I'll bid my true value of $25 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding my true value ensures I only win when profitable (value ≥ second-highest bid) and never overpay. With a value of $3, I should bid exactly $3 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (Vickrey auction), where the winner pays the second-highest bid rather than their own bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win with a high second-highest bid. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $26, bidding $26 truthfully maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid.
